text: Prior work by Kaal shows that Dodd-Frank Act registration and increased compliance requirements only marginally increase the cost structure of private funds, and finds non-robust evidence that higher administrative costs are a second-order effect that does not affect overall private fund returns.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408

isBasedOn.name: Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015

abstract: Kaal (2013a, 2015c) finds non-robust evidence that the higher administrative costs imposed by the Dodd-Frank Act are a second-order effect of the regulation, thereby not affecting the overall returns of private funds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: prior survey and cost data in Kaal 2013a, 2015b, 2015c, 2016
